classification.difficultyReason: Combine the two supplied shaded pictures using either-region or both-region membership; the complement is already represented visually.

content.prompt: The two Venn diagrams show $A$ and $B'$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6, supplied diagram pair above parts a and b
spec.description: Two diagrams in one horizontal comparison strip, headed A and B′. Ordinary outlines and labels are black; source grey membership shading uses the restrained house blue fill.
spec.mathematics: Left: all of A, including A ∩ B, is shaded. Right: the entire universal rectangle outside B is shaded, including A-only and neither.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied givens, visible in the question edition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Shade $A \cup B'$ by shading everything that is either in the first picture or in the second picture.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular universal set with overlapping circles, A on the left and B on the right.
spec.mathematics: Four regions: A-only, A ∩ B, B-only and neither.
spec.answerVisibility: Student shading response; completed source shading is withheld.

answer.worked: The union includes every region shaded in either supplied diagram. Shade all of $A$ and everything outside $B$: the $A$-only region, the overlap and the region outside both circles. Leave only $B \cap A'$ unshaded.

spec.description: Complete solution figure with light blue shading everywhere except the B-only region.
spec.mathematics: A ∪ B′ contains A-only, A ∩ B and neither; B-only is excluded.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Shade $A \cap B'$ by shading anything that is in both the first and second picture.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular universal set with overlapping circles, A on the left and B on the right.
spec.mathematics: Four regions: A-only, A ∩ B, B-only and neither.
spec.answerVisibility: Student shading response; completed source shading is withheld.

answer.worked: The intersection includes only regions shaded in both supplied diagrams. These points are in $A$ and outside $B$, so shade only the $A$-only region and leave the overlap unshaded.

spec.description: Complete solution figure with only the A-only region shaded light blue.
spec.mathematics: A ∩ B′ = A \ B; the overlap, B-only and neither are unshaded.
